claims.text: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr is the alloy system being processed.
Ti powder is an effective oxygen getter for this hydride-based HfNbTaTiZr process.
A Ti-getter dose of 5-10 wt% relative to estimated oxygen ingress is sufficient.
Heating at 100-200 °C/min to 1350-1400 °C will completely decompose the listed hydrides and homogenize the alloy.
Quenching faster than 300 °C/min will suppress alpha-BCC and HCP formation and retain a single beta-BCC phase.
The beta-BCC phase is thermodynamically stable at high temperature but metastable at room temperature.
HIP processing of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr can produce a secondary HCP phase in addition to the BCC matrix.
Slow cooling permits a eutectoid decomposition of beta-BCC into alpha-BCC and HCP phases.
Oxygen stabilization is responsible for the HCP and alpha-BCC phases found after slow cooling or HIP.
The Ti getter reacts with oxygen and potentially hydrogen to form TiO2 and TiH2.
An oxygen concentration around or above 0.8 wt% triggers HCP formation and embrittlement in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed getter and thermal cycle will maintain bulk oxygen below 0.15 wt%.
Keeping oxygen below 0.15 wt% will prevent HfO2 precipitation and oxygen-stabilized phases.
The rapidly quenched microstructure will have a grain size of 10-20 μm.
Rapid thermal cycling and gas evolution during hydride decomposition will refine grains by increasing nucleation density.
SPS-only HfNbTaTiZr has an approximately 50 μm grain size, whereas HPT-processed material has sub-micron grains.
The proposed product will achieve greater than 98% density.
The proposed product will have a Vickers hardness of approximately 350-400 HV.
Insufficient peak temperature will leave hydride residues incompletely dissolved and cause porosity.
If cooling is slower than 300 °C/min or oxygen exceeds 0.8 wt%, beta-BCC will decompose into alpha-BCC and HCP phases.

contradictions.description: The mechanism and baseline predict HCP formation during slow cooling, but falsification rule (1) says that detecting HCP during the slow-cooling run falsifies the hypothesis. That observation would instead support the stated slow-cooling mechanism.
The boundary predicts alpha-BCC/HCP formation when gettering is absent or oxygen exceeds 0.8 wt%, whereas falsification rule (3) treats alpha-BCC formation under those same conditions as falsifying.
